title: O, Come, Loud Anthems Let Us Sing
description: O, Come, Loud Anthems Let Us Sing in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 5 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, Come, loud an-thems let us sing, Loud thanks to our Al-might-y King; For we our voi-ces high should raise, When our sal-va-tion's Rock we praise.

lines: O, Come, loud anthems let us sing,
Loud thanks to our Almighty King;
For we our voices high should raise,
When our salvation's Rock we praise.
Into his presence let us haste,
To thank him, for his favors past;
To him address, in joyful songs,
The praise that to his name belongs.
O, let us to his courts repair,
With joy and fear devoutly all
Before the Lord, our Maker, fall!

licence: Public domain: Nahum Tate died in 1715; Nicholas Brady died in 1726.
credits: Words by Nahum Tate (1652–1715) and Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
